title: Falsifier verdicts
description: The verdict record a reconciliation run writes on its lifecycle Batch (metadata.verdicts) beside its candidate record (req-grid-reconcile-falsifier). One entry per retirement candidate: the verdict the candidate's type's falsifier returned, or the fact that the type has no falsifier and is therefore not reconcilable. Authority is off: this record retires, renames and unlinks nothing; each entry names the write the reconcile verb WOULD make and its one home, so the plan is readable before anything acts on it.

recorded_at.description: When the dispatch ran and this record was written (UTC, ISO 8601).

authority.description: Whether anything acted on these verdicts. Only 'off' exists: the reconcile verb's run-config authority (req-grid-reconcile-verb) is not built, so this record licenses nothing and nothing reads it to retire.

candidates.description: How many candidates the run's candidate record held — the number of entries below.

calls.description: How many times each entity type's falsifier was called: exactly 1 per type that has one, because batch is the interface (one call for fifty candidates, never fifty calls). A type with no falsifier has no key here.

stray_answers.description: Per entity type, how many answers the falsifier returned for ids it was not asked about (or that were not Verdict objects). Dropped, never recorded as verdicts; a non-zero count is a falsifier defect worth a look. A type with none has no key here.

not_reconcilable.description: The entity types among the candidates that have no registered falsifier, sorted. Their candidates are recorded as not re-observed and are never probed or retired (req-grid-reconcile-falsifier-1).

entries.description: One entry per candidate, ordered by candidate-record surface index, then entity type, then entity id.

entity_id.description: The candidate's entity id, as the candidate record holds it.

entity_type.description: The candidate's entity type slug — the key the falsifier was chosen by.

candidate_reason.description: The retirement reason the candidate record derived (why it is a candidate at all), copied verbatim.

surface.description: Index into the candidate record's surfaces array: which listing this candidate fell out of.

outcome.description: judged: the type's falsifier was called and answered (verdict is set). not_reconcilable: no falsifier is registered for the type; the candidate was not probed and is recorded as not re-observed (verdict is null).

verdict.description: The falsifier's verdict, one of the five in the spec, or null when the entry is not_reconcilable. DROPPED_FROM_OBSERVATION: listing and probe agree it is gone. PRESENT_AT_PROBE: the probe found the same source identity under the same owner (see statement and cause). RELOCATED: same identity, new name or different owner (see kind). UNDETERMINED: the probe could not answer (see reason). REIDENTIFIED: a different source identity at the same address.

reason.description: For UNDETERMINED only: why the probe could not answer. errored also covers a falsifier that raised or returned no verdict for the candidate — recorded fail-closed, never retired. Null otherwise.

kind.description: For RELOCATED only: renamed = same source identity and owner under a new name (a locator update, req-grid-reconcile-falsifier-8); transferred = same source identity under a different owner (ends this owner's relationship only, -7/-9). Null otherwise.

cause.description: For PRESENT_AT_PROBE only: created_after_listing_started when the source's creation time is at or after the surface's observation interval start (timing rules this cause IN); indeterminate otherwise, because restored access explains it equally well. Frequency never classifies cause (req-grid-reconcile-falsifier-4). Null otherwise.

statement.description: For PRESENT_AT_PROBE only: the disjunction, stated in full — created after the listing started OR access restored between listing and probe. It never asserts a collector defect. Null otherwise.

probe.description: A summary of what the probe returned, in source terms, so the verdict can be checked against its evidence. Null when no probe ran (not_reconcilable, or a falsifier that raised).

status.description: Whether the probe found the object, found nothing, or could not answer (and why).

source_id.description: The stable source identity the probe returned, when found.

owner.description: The owner or containing scope the probe returned, when found.

name.description: The name or locator the probe returned, when found.

created_at.description: The source's creation time for the object, when it reports one.

detail.description: Free text from the probe (an error message, a rate-limit header), for a human; never read by the dispatch.

expected.description: The grid-side terms the falsifier compared the probe against — what the grid holds for the candidate, in the source's own terms. Recorded so the dispatch can re-derive the classification from both sides and refuse a verdict they do not yield. Null when no comparison was made (not_reconcilable, a failed probe, a falsifier that raised).

source_id.description: The stable source identity the natural key rests on.

owner.description: The owner or containing scope the object was observed under.

name.description: The name or locator the grid holds.

note.description: The falsifier's or the dispatch's own note on this entry, for a human. Empty when there is nothing to say.

would.description: The write the reconcile verb WOULD make on this verdict with authority on, and its one home (req-grid-reconcile-falsifier-3). Nothing here has been done.

write.description: tombstone: retire the entity (DROPPED_FROM_OBSERVATION). rename: update the entity's name (RELOCATED renamed). end_ownership_edge: retire this owner's edge to the entity, leaving the entity and its children live (RELOCATED transferred). none: a run-record entry only (PRESENT_AT_PROBE, UNDETERMINED, REIDENTIFIED, not_reconcilable).

home.description: Where that write lands. Each verdict has exactly one home.
